patches.why: `?stainless_overload=branchFrom` is how the spec's generator (Stainless) gives one path and method a second client method; it is not a parameter of turbopuffer's. Turbopuffer's documentation names no such parameter and branches a namespace with a `branch_from_namespace` field in the body of POST /v2/namespaces/:namespace (https://turbopuffer.com/docs/branching.md, the page as turbopuffer publishes it for readers other than a browser, whose curl example posts that body to the plain path), which the spec's own Write body already has (`BranchFromNamespaceParams`). The official client sends the key with that same body, `{ branch_from_namespace: body }` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/turbopuffer/turbopuffer-typescript/v2.8.0/src/resources/namespaces.ts, `branchFrom`), so the twin serves it as the write operation and ignores the key. That turbopuffer's server ignores the key too is inferred from the documentation, not observed.

value.description: (Optional) The encryption configuration for the destination namespace.

patches.why: The spec's copyFrom overload (removed below) says a copy's body carries `dest_encryption` beside `source_namespace`, and the official client sends the whole of it inside `copy_from_namespace` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/turbopuffer/turbopuffer-typescript/v2.8.0/src/resources/namespaces.ts, `copyFrom`: `body: { copy_from_namespace: body }`); the Write body's `CopyFromNamespaceConfig` lacks it, so it moves there before the overload goes.

As for branchFrom: `?stainless_overload=copyFrom` is the spec generator's device, not a turbopuffer parameter. Turbopuffer copies a namespace with a `copy_from_namespace` field in the body of POST /v2/namespaces/:namespace (https://turbopuffer.com/docs/write: "The client libraries expose a copy_from() / copyFrom() convenience method that wraps this parameter"; its curl example posts that body to the plain path), which the spec's Write body already has (`CopyFromNamespaceParams`). The official client sends the key with that body (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/turbopuffer/turbopuffer-typescript/v2.8.0/src/resources/namespaces.ts, `copyFrom`), so the twin serves it as the write operation and ignores the key. That turbopuffer's server ignores the key is inferred from the documentation, not observed.

source.quote: The client libraries expose a copy_from() / copyFrom() convenience method that wraps this parameter.

rerank_by.description: How to combine the rows returned by each sub-query into a single ranked list.

patches.why: Turbopuffer's query endpoint takes a multi-query in its own body: "You can provide multiple query objects to be executed simultaneously on a namespace", with a curl example posting `{"queries": [...]}` to POST /v2/namespaces/:namespace/query (https://turbopuffer.com/docs/query.md, the page as turbopuffer publishes it for readers other than a browser; its HTML renders the Python example first). The spec gives that body to a pseudo-path `?stainless_overload=multiQuery` (removed below) that the official client sends it to (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/turbopuffer/turbopuffer-typescript/v2.8.0/src/resources/namespaces.ts, `multiQuery`), so the query operation takes either body.

A multi-query sent to the query endpoint answers its results per sub-query (the spec's MultiQueryResult, which the multiQuery pseudo-path answered); a single query answers QueryResult (https://turbopuffer.com/docs/query).

source.quote: Individual sub-queries can vary their parameters independently

patches.why: `?stainless_overload=multiQuery` is the spec generator's device for a second client method on one path, not a turbopuffer parameter (https://turbopuffer.com/docs/query names none, and posts a multi-query to the plain path). Its body and answer now belong to the query operation (the two patches above); the official client still sends the key (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/turbopuffer/turbopuffer-typescript/v2.8.0/src/resources/namespaces.ts, `multiQuery`), and the twin ignores it. That turbopuffer's server ignores the key is inferred from the documentation, not observed.

source.quote: Multi-queries offer better performance than issuing independent queries to the same namespace.

patches.why: turbopuffer's Namespace metadata page documents the read at GET /v1/namespaces/:namespace/metadata, and its curl example reads it there; the spec has only GET /v2/namespaces/{namespace}/metadata (which the client sends) beside PATCH at the /v1 path. Both paths answer the same metadata.

value.description: The timestamp when the namespace's data was last modified.

patches.why: The Namespace metadata page answers `last_write_at`, "The timestamp when the namespace's data was last modified", beside `updated_at` (data or schema); the spec's NamespaceMetadata omits it.

source.quote: The timestamp when the namespace's data was last modified, in ISO 8601 format.

value.description: The state of branching for the namespace. Only present for branched namespaces.

parent.description: The namespace this was branched from.

patches.why: The Namespace metadata page answers `branching` for a branched namespace (`parent`, the namespace it was branched from); the spec's NamespaceMetadata omits it.

source.quote: The namespace this was branched from.

value.description: The timestamp of the last write operation that the query observed.

patches.why: The Query page's response lists `last_included_write_at` among a query's performance fields; the spec's QueryPerformance omits it.

source.quote: the timestamp of the last write operation that the query observed

200.description: The operation's status, and its result once it has finished.

patches.why: turbopuffer's API overview documents asynchronous requests: a Prefer: respond-async request is answered 202 with a Location to poll, `GET /v1/namespaces/<ns>/operations/<token>` in its curl example, whose answers are `{"status": "running"}` or `{"status": "finished", "result": {"success": …} | {"error": {"status_code", "detail"}}}` (the Write page's copy-progress example adds `progress`). The vendored spec has no such path.

source.quote: Poll that location to check on progress

value.description: The operation was started in the background (Prefer: respond-async).

patches.why: A copy_from_namespace write sent with Prefer: respond-async is answered `202 Accepted` with a `Location` header and `{"token": "tpuf-abc123"}` (the API overview's example); the spec gives the write no 202.

source.quote: The server returns `202 Accepted` with a `Location` header pointing to the operation.
